name: Bill Shankly
description: Liverpool manager in his golden era: a team with its own identity, high pressing and great intensity, guided by simple play and patience.

name: Fernando Diniz
description: Possession coach with short passing and position rotation, who values technique, aesthetics and the team's identity above a fixed system.

name: José Mourinho
description: Pragmatic coach who organises the team around a disciplined system, defensive solidity and results, adapting the plan to each opponent.

name: Jürgen Klopp
description: Coach of counter-pressing and quick transitions, with a team that presses high, plays vertically after winning the ball and has great physical intensity.

name: Marcelo Bielsa
description: Coach obsessed with his own game plan: very high pressing, man-marking, vertical attack and a style that does not change with the opponent.

name: Pep Guardiola
description: Possession and positional-play coach who builds patiently, occupies space with purpose and presses high to win the ball back.

name: Renato Gaúcho
description: Coach who does not treat possession as an end in itself: plays fast and direct with real wingers, changes the plan for each opponent and gives his stars freedom.

name: Telê Santana
description: Coach of Brazilian futebol-arte: prefers technique and talent, gives his stars freedom and cares about spectacle without giving up on winning.

name: Arrigo Sacchi
description: Coach of the Milan side of Van Basten and Gullit: collective high pressing, zonal marking and a high defensive line, with a system above the stars.

name: Rinus Michels
description: Creator of total football at Ajax and Barcelona: a fluid 4-3-3, positional interchange, the offside trap and pressing to win the ball back.

name: Louis van Gaal
description: Coach of the Ajax side that won the 1995 Champions League, built on possession, attack and youth, and of Barcelona, Spanish champions.

name: Alex Ferguson
description: Manchester United manager for over 26 years: wing play, man-marking, a focus on results and authority, with the club's identity above each opponent.

name: Arsène Wenger
description: Arsenal manager of short passes and combinations through the middle, with his own identity, technical talent and the unbeaten 2003-04 side.

name: Carlo Ancelotti
description: Pragmatic, adaptable coach: a midfield diamond, freedom for the stars, a mid block and a focus on results, with harmony in the squad.

name: Diego Simeone
description: Coach of a compact block and direct counter-attacks, with a system above talent, an imposed identity and authority in the dressing room.

name: Massimiliano Allegri
description: Pragmatic coach focused on results: counter-attacks, a deep block and trust in his stars, adapting the plan without giving up on winning.

name: Miguel Cardoso
description: Possession coach with a high block and positional play at Mamelodi Sundowns, South African and African Champions League winner.

name: Pedro Emanuel
description: Results-driven coach with a fixed system and zonal marking, not tied to possession: Taça de Portugal and Saudi King's Cup winner.

name: Cláudio Coutinho
description: Brazil coach at the 1978 World Cup and the 1980 Flamengo champions: system above talent, total football imported from Michels, physical and disciplined.

name: Stan Cullis
description: Wolves manager for 16 years: direct, fast, physical football built on intense preparation and discipline.

name: Hugo Meisl
description: Austria's national coach from 1913 to 1937, who built the Wunderteam, the showcase of the Danubian short-passing school.

name: Herbert Chapman
description: Huddersfield and Arsenal manager: created the WM, with the stopper and the counter-attack, and won English titles.

name: Gusztáv Sebes
description: Hungary's national coach until 1956: brought the withdrawn centre-forward to the national team and built the side around a few clubs, above all Honvéd.

name: Renato Cesarini
description: River Plate coach in 1941, when La Máquina took shape, and Juventus coach in 1959–60.

name: César Luis Menotti
description: Manager of Huracán and of Argentina, 1978 World Cup winners, who defended attacking, possession football with technical players free to create.

name: Carlos Bilardo
description: Manager of Estudiantes and of Argentina, 1986 World Cup winners: pragmatic and obsessed with results, with man-marking and a plan adjusted to each opponent.

name: Osvaldo Zubeldía
description: Manager of Estudiantes, three-time Libertadores winners (1968–70), who built a reactive and highly competitive side on organisation, discipline and detailed training.

name: Marcelo Gallardo
description: River Plate manager from 2014 to 2022: a possession-based, high-pressing team with its own identity and many titles, including two Libertadores.

name: Johan Cruyff
description: Manager of Ajax and of the Barcelona Dream Team: possession, positional play and an attacking identity above the opponent, with technique as the foundation.

name: Helenio Herrera
description: Manager of Inter in the 1960s and a symbol of catenaccio: an organised defence, fast counter-attacks, strict discipline and strong leadership.

name: Valeriy Lobanovskyi
description: Manager of Dynamo Kyiv and the Soviet Union, a pioneer of the scientific approach: collective pressing, system above individuals and total authority.

name: Ralf Rangnick
description: Manager of Hoffenheim and RB Leipzig and a reference for gegenpressing: very high pressing, fast transitions, vertical play and a well-defined system.

name: Carlos Bianchi
description: Manager of Vélez and Boca Juniors, winner of the Libertadores and the Intercontinental Cup: a compact, pragmatic and efficient team, with a firm hand over the squad.

name: Luiz Felipe Scolari
description: Manager of Grêmio, of Brazil, 2002 World Cup winners, and of Portugal: an organised, pragmatic team with a united group and results first.

name: Abel Ferreira
description: Palmeiras manager since 2020: a solid, pragmatic team that adapts to the opponent, with strong defensive organisation and firm command of the squad.

name: Antonio Conte
description: Manager of Chelsea and Inter: a back three with man-marking, fast transitions, an experienced squad and demanding leadership.

name: Tite
description: Manager of the Brazilian national team: collective organisation, possession, zonal marking and adapting to the game, with good squad management.

name: Jorge Sampaoli
description: Manager of Universidad de Chile and of Chile, 2015 Copa América winners, a disciple of Bielsa: high pressing, man-marking and intense attacking play.

name: Óscar Tabárez
description: Uruguay national team manager for 15 years: a compact, reactive side that played down the flanks with a strong sense of group, from fourth place in 2010 to the 2011 Copa América.

name: Francisco Maturana
description: Manager of Atlético Nacional, 1989 Libertadores winners, and of Colombia in the 1990s: possession with short passing, wide attacks and freedom for the stars.

name: Bob Paisley
description: Liverpool manager and three-time European champion: a patient, collective team with a high line and its own game plan, relying on an experienced squad.

name: Brian Clough
description: Manager of Derby County and Nottingham Forest, twice European champions: passing on the ground, simple play and total authority over the players.

name: Ernst Happel
description: Manager of Feyenoord, Club Brugge, the Netherlands and Hamburg, European champion with two clubs: pressing, zonal marking and the authority to impose his own style.

name: Jorge Jesus
description: Manager of Benfica and of Flamengo in 2019: vertical play, intense pressing, his own style and strict control over an experienced squad.

name: Luis Aragonés
description: Manager of Atlético Madrid and of Spain, Euro 2008 winners: pragmatic possession, direct play when needed and a strong personality.

name: Vicente del Bosque
description: Manager of Spain, 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 winners: control with the ball, a high line, a harmonious dressing room and calm management of great players.

name: Zdeněk Zeman
description: Manager of Foggia, Lazio and Roma: attacking, spectacular football, high pressing, zonal marking and strict physical discipline, betting on young players.

name: Xabi Alonso
description: Manager of the Bayer Leverkusen side that won the unbeaten 2023–24 Bundesliga: positional play, progression through the middle and a system worth more than its stars.

name: Mário Zagallo
description: Manager of the Brazilian national team, 1970 World Cup winners: a disciplined, results-driven side with a fluid attack through the middle and a low block when needed.

name: Vanderlei Luxemburgo
description: Manager of Palmeiras, Corinthians, Cruzeiro and Santos, several times Brazilian champion: a pragmatic team with a diamond midfield and strong command.

name: Claudio Ranieri
description: Manager of Leicester, English champions in 2016: a compact 4-4-2, zonal marking, fast counter-attacks and a focus on results, with an experienced squad.

name: Jupp Heynckes
description: Manager of Bayern Munich's 2013 treble: a balance between attack and defence, a compact block, wing play and calm authority.

name: Simone Inzaghi
description: Manager of Lazio and Inter: a drilled 3-5-2, wide wing-backs, a mid or low block and fast transitions, with an experienced squad.

name: Rafael Benítez
description: Manager of Valencia and of Liverpool, European champions in 2005: zonal marking, preparation for each opponent, squad rotation and authority.

name: Hansi Flick
description: Manager of Bayern Munich and Barcelona: a very high line, pressing straight after losing the ball, wing play, trust in young players and authority with respect.

name: Thomas Tuchel
description: Manager of Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Bayern: a different plan for each match, build-up through the middle, zonal marking and authority over the group.

name: Didier Deschamps
description: Manager of the France national team, 2018 World Cup winners: a low block, counter-attacks, a focus on results, adapting to the opponent and authority over the group.

name: Lionel Scaloni
description: Manager of Argentina, 2022 World Cup winners: man-marking, a high press, a plan that changes with each opponent and a united group around Messi.
